title: 60% Tax Trap Calculator 2026/27: the £100k Trap
description: See what the £100k tax trap costs you in 2026/27 and the exact pension contribution, by salary sacrifice or SIPP, that gets you back to £100,000.
intro: Work out your income tax, National Insurance and lost Personal Allowance between £100,000 and £125,140, and how much pension it takes to get out of the 60% band.
differentiator: Shows the Personal Allowance taper step by step with income tax by band and employee NI for 2026/27, then the exact salary sacrifice and relief at source (grossed-up) contribution that brings adjusted net income to £100,000, with the take-home cost of each, plus the £100,000 childcare cliff flag.

sources.title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances
sources.note: 2026 to 2027 Personal Allowance £12,570, bands 20%/40%/45%, additional rate over £125,140, allowance reduced £1 for every £2 of adjusted net income over £100,000 and zero from £125,140.

sources.title: Income Tax rates and allowances for current and past years
sources.note: 2026 to 2027 basic rate band £37,700 of taxable income, higher rate £37,701 to £125,140, income limit for Personal Allowance £100,000.

sources.title: Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027
sources.note: Class 1 primary threshold £12,570 and upper earnings limit £50,270 a year; employee category A rates 8% and 2%.

sources.title: Adjusted net income
sources.note: How adjusted net income is worked out: gross pension payments off, then relief at source pension contributions and Gift Aid grossed up (£1.25 for every £1).

sources.title: PTM056120: rate of tax charge, terms used
sources.note: Both the basic rate limit and the higher rate limit are increased by the gross amount of relief at source contributions and Gift Aid.

sources.title: Tax on your private pension: pension tax relief
sources.note: Relief at source: the provider claims 20% and adds it to the pot; higher rate taxpayers claim the rest through Self Assessment.

sources.title: Salary sacrifice and the effects on PAYE
sources.note: Salary sacrifice reduces the cash pay that income tax and NI are charged on; employer pension contributions are not taxed as a benefit.

sources.title: Maintaining Income Tax and equivalent NIC thresholds until 5 April 2031
sources.note: Personal Allowance £12,570, basic rate limit £37,700, and the NI primary threshold and upper earnings limit held until 5 April 2031 (Budget 2025).

sources.title: Tax-Free Childcare: check if you're eligible
sources.note: Not eligible if you or your partner's expected adjusted net income is over £100,000 for the current tax year.

sources.title: Tax-Free Childcare
sources.note: £2 top-up for every £8 paid in, up to £500 every 3 months (£2,000 a year) per child, or £1,000 (£4,000 a year) for a disabled child.

sources.title: Free childcare for working parents: check if you're eligible
sources.note: England: 30 hours a week for 38 weeks for children aged 9 months to 4 years; not eligible if either parent's expected adjusted net income is over £100,000.

faqs.a: Between £100,000 and £125,140 of adjusted net income your Personal Allowance shrinks by £1 for every £2 you earn. Each extra pound is taxed at 40% and also drags 50p of allowance into tax at 40%, so the effective income tax rate is 60%, plus 2% National Insurance for employees.

faqs.q: How do I avoid the 100k tax trap?
faqs.a: Reduce your adjusted net income to £100,000 or less. The usual ways are salary sacrifice into a workplace pension, a personal pension contribution under relief at source (each £1 paid counts as £1.25), or Gift Aid donations, which are grossed up the same way.

faqs.q: How much pension do I need to pay to get under £100,000?
faqs.a: By salary sacrifice, the full amount you are over. With a relief at source personal pension, you pay 80% of the amount you are over, because the provider adds basic rate relief. On a £110,000 salary that is £10,000 sacrificed, or £8,000 paid in.

faqs.q: Does the £100k tax trap affect childcare?
faqs.a: Yes. If you or your partner expect adjusted net income over £100,000 for the tax year, you lose Tax-Free Childcare, worth up to £2,000 per child a year, and in England the working-parent free childcare hours. Getting to £100,000 or less restores eligibility.

faqs.q: Is the 60% tax trap the same in Scotland?
faqs.a: The Personal Allowance taper applies in Scotland too, but Scottish income tax bands and rates are different, so the marginal rate inside the taper is different there. This calculator uses the bands for England, Wales and Northern Ireland only.

GOV.UK lists the same £100,000 income limit for 2025 to 2026 and 2026 to 2027. The Personal Allowance, basic rate limit and NI thresholds are frozen until 5 April 2031 under Budget 2025, so more earners reach the taper as pay rises.
